name: ADRENOCORTICOTROPIC HORMONE
description: ACTH measures pituitary gland function and helps evaluate the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. This test diagnoses Cushing's disease, Addison's disease, and pituitary disorders affecting ACTH secretion.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Siemens Immulite

literatureReview: ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic Hormone) is produced by the pituitary gland and stimulates cortisol production by the adrenal cortex. Normal morning range is 7.2-46 pg/mL. Elevated levels suggest pituitary Cushing's disease or ectopic ACTH production. Low levels indicate pituitary insufficiency or exogenous steroid suppression. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides high sensitivity for this low-concentration hormone. Samples must be collected in chilled EDTA tubes and centrifuged immediately to prevent degradation. ACTH has a pulsatile secretion pattern, so timing is important. Used with cortisol levels to differentiate causes of adrenal dysfunction. Critical for diagnosing pituitary vs adrenal pathology in cortisol disorders.
